reasoning_content:
1.5 GB download — at roughly 6 MB/s that'd be about 4–5 minutes. Within tolerance. Let's download to /opt and extract. The tarball contains an `android-studio/` directory at the top level (the rabbit1 layout: an android-studio directory containing bin, jbr, lib, etc.).

Let's run the download in the background so I can make progress on other work in the meantime… actually, no, I need it before the final doctor. Let me set a sufficient timeout and run it in the foreground (the command timeout is 600 seconds = 10 minutes). 1.5GB at 6.5MB/s ≈ 4 minutes. OK.

action.command: cd /opt && curl -sL --max-time 580 -o studio.tar.gz "https://edgedl.me.gvt1.com/android/studio/ide-zips/2026.2.1.8/android-studio-rabbit1-linux.tar.gz" && ls -la studio.tar.gz && tar xzf studio.tar.gz && ls /opt/ && ls android-studio/ | head
